title: Bekhorot 57
description: Rabbi Yoḥanan’s brothers who are purchasers, the partners who split ten lambs against nine and a dog, the animals that do and do not enter the tithing pen, Rabbi Yishmael ben Satriel’s wonders of Arkat Leveina, and the three gathering times for animal tithe.
topics: 👬 Brothers who divided are purchasers: why Rabbi Yoḥanan had to say it of both the field and the flock
🐕 Ten lambs against nine and a dog: Rav Ashi’s “small amount” that runs through all of them
🚪 What may not enter the pen: diverse kinds, a tereifa, a caesarean birth, one too young, an orphan
📜 “Under the rod” and “under its mother”: the verbal analogy from offerings, and the “corruption” that is like a blemish
⚧ The tumtum and the hermaphrodite in the pen: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda’s dissent
🥬 Lettuce of 600,000 leaves, a cedar sixteen wagons wide, and the egg of the bar yokhani
📅 Three gathering times for animal tithe: Rabbi Akiva, Ben Azzai, Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon, and Rabbi Meir’s new year

a1.he: וְאַזְדָּא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָאַחִין שֶׁחָלְקוּ — לָקוֹחוֹת הֵן, וּמַחְזִירִין זֶה לָזֶה בַּיּוֹבֵל.

a2.he: וּצְרִיכִי, דְּאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן הָכָא, בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דּוּמְיָא דְּבִנְךָ, מָה בִּנְךָ בְּבָרוּר לָךְ, אַף שׁוֹרְךָ וְצֹאנְךָ בְּבָרוּר לָךְ; אֲבָל שָׂדֶה מֶכֶר הוּא דְּאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא לֶיהְדַּר בְּיוֹבֵל, יְרוּשָּׁה וּמַתָּנָה לָא!

a3.he: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן שָׂדֶה — לְחוּמְרָא, אִי נָמֵי לְכַתְּחִלָּה, אֲבָל הָכָא — אֵימָא לָא, צְרִיכָא.

a4.he: מֵיתִיבִי: וְכֵן הַשּׁוּתָּפִין שֶׁחָלְקוּ, אֶחָד נָטַל עֲשָׂרָה וְאֶחָד נָטַל תִּשְׁעָה וָכֶלֶב — שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד הַכֶּלֶב אֲסוּרִין, שֶׁעִם הַכֶּלֶב מוּתָּרִים. וְאִם אָמְרַתְּ יֵשׁ בְּרֵירָה, לִיבְרוֹר חַד מִינַּיְיהוּ לְבַהֲדֵי כֶלֶב וְלִשְׁקוֹל, וְהָנָךְ לִישְׁתְּרוֹ!

a5.he: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אִי דְּשָׁווּ כּוּלְּהוּ לַהֲדָדֵי — הָכִי נָמֵי, הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? דְּלָא שָׁווּ כּוּלְּהוּ לַהֲדָדֵי, וְשָׁוֵי הַאי כַּלְבָּא חַד וּמַשֶּׁהוּ, וְהַאי מַשֶּׁהוּ מָשֵׁיךְ וְאָתֵי בְּכוּלְּהוּ.

a6.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַכֹּל נִכְנָסִין לַדִּיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר, חוּץ מִן כִּלְאַיִם, וּטְרֵפָה, וְיוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן, וּמְחוּסַּר זְמַן, וְהַיָּתוֹם. וְאֵיזֶהוּ יָתוֹם? כֹּל שֶׁמֵּתָה אִמָּהּ שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ יָלְדָה. רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ נִשְׁחֲטָה אִמָּהּ וְהַשֶּׁלַח קַיָּים — אֵין זֶה יָתוֹם.

a7.he: גְּמָ׳ מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״שׁוֹר אוֹ כֶשֶׂב״ — פְּרָט לְכִלְאַיִם, ״אוֹ עֵז״ — פְּרָט לְנִדְמֶה, ״כִּי יִוָּלֵד״ — פְּרָט לְיוֹצֵא דוֹפֶן, ״וְהָיָה שִׁבְעַת יָמִים״ — פְּרָט לִמְחוּסַּר זְמַן, ״תַּחַת אִמּוֹ״ — פְּרָט לְיָתוֹם.

a8.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט״, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן ״תַּחַת אִמּוֹ״. מָה לְהַלָּן — פְּרָט לְכׇל הַשֵּׁמוֹת הַלָּלוּ, אַף כָּאן — פְּרָט לְכׇל הַשֵּׁמוֹת הַלָּלוּ. וּמָה כָּאן — פְּרָט לִטְרֵפָה, אַף לְהַלָּן — פְּרָט לִטְרֵפָה.

a9.he: ״הַכֹּל״, לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵיתוֹיֵי הָא דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָרוֹבֵעַ, וְהַנִּרְבָּע, וְהַמּוּקְצֶה, וְהַנֶּעֱבָד, וְהָאֶתְנַן, וְהַמְחִיר, וְטוּמְטוּם, וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס — כּוּלָּן נִכְנָסִין לַדִּיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס אֵין נִכְנָסִין לַדִּיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר.

a10.he: וְתַנָּא דִּידַן, אִי גָּמַר ״תַּחַת״ ״תַּחַת״ מִקֳּדָשִׁים — הָנֵי נָמֵי לָא, וְאִי לָא יָלֵיף — הָנֵי מְנָא לֵיהּ?

a11.he: לְעוֹלָם גָּמַיר, וְהָנֵי רַחֲמָנָא רַבִּינְהוּ, דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי מׇשְׁחָתָם בָּהֶם מוּם בָּם לֹא יֵרָצוּ לָכֶם״, וְתָאנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ הַשְׁחָתָה, אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא דְּבַר עֶרְוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.

a12.he: דְּבַר עֶרְוָה — דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי הִשְׁחִית כׇּל בָּשָׂר אֶת דַּרְכּוֹ עַל הָאָרֶץ״, עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה — דִּכְתִיב: ״פֶּן תַּשְׁחִיתוּן וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לָכֶם פֶּסֶל תְּמוּנַת כׇּל סָמֶל תַּבְנִית זָכָר אוֹ נְקֵבָה״.

a13.he: וְכֹל שֶׁהַמּוּם פּוֹסֵל בּוֹ — דְּבַר עֶרְוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה פּוֹסְלִין בּוֹ, וְכֹל שֶׁאֵין הַמּוּם פּוֹסֵל בּוֹ — אֵין דְּבַר עֶרְוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה פּוֹסְלִין בּוֹ, וְהַאי מַעֲשֵׂר הוֹאִיל וְלָא פָּסֵיל בֵּיהּ מוּמָא, דִּכְתִיב: ״לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין טוֹב לָרַע וְלֹא יְמִירֶנּוּ״ — דְּבַר עֶרְוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה נָמֵי לָא פָּסֵיל בֵּיהּ.

a14.he: רוֹבֵעַ וְנִרְבָּע — דְּבַר עֶרְוָה, מוּקְצֶה וְנֶעֱבָד — עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וְאֶתְנַן — דְּבַר עֶרְוָה, וּמְחִיר אִיתַּקַּשׁ לְאֶתְנַן,

a16.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר. קָסָבַר סְפֵיקָא הוּא, מִיעֵט רַחֲמָנָא גַּבֵּי קָדָשִׁים — זָכָר וַדַּאי וּנְקֵבָה וַדָּאִית, וְלֹא טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס. מַעֲשֵׂר נָמֵי גְּמַר ״תַּחַת״ ״תַּחַת״ מִקֳּדָשִׁים.

a17.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַכֹּל נִכְנָסִין לַדִּיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר, חוּץ מִן הַכִּלְאַיִם וְהַטְּרֵפָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אִישׁ כְּפַר בַּרְתּוֹתָא שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ. אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אֲנִי שָׁמַעְתִּי הֵימֶנּוּ אַף יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן וּמְחוּסַּר זְמַן וְיָתוֹם.

a18.he: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא, אִי גָּמַר ״תַּחַת״ ״תַּחַת״ מִקֳּדָשִׁים — הָנֵי נָמֵי לָא, וְאִי לָא גָּמַר, בִּשְׁלָמָא טְרֵפָה — ״כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט״ כְּתִיב, פְּרָט לִטְרֵפָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ עוֹבֶרֶת, אֶלָּא כִּלְאַיִם מְנָא לֵיהּ?

b1.he: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, דְּאָמַר: יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן — וָלָד מְעַלְּיָא הוּא, וּדְלָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן.

b2.he: בִּמְחוּסַּר זְמַן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה, יָתוֹם — כְּגוֹן שֶׁהַשֶּׁלַח קַיָּים, וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ שָׁחַט אֶת אִמּוֹ וְהַשֶּׁלַח קַיָּים — אֵין זֶה יָתוֹם.

b3.he: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן סַתְרִיאֵל מֵעַרְקַת לִבְנָה לִפְנֵי רַבִּי: בִּמְקוֹמֵנוּ מַפְשִׁיטִין אֶת הַמֵּתָה וּמַלְבִּישִׁין אֶת הַחַי. אָמַר רַבִּי: נִתְגַּלָּה טַעְמָהּ שֶׁל מִשְׁנָתֵינוּ.

b4.he: חֲזֵירִין שֶׁבִּמְקוֹמֵנוּ יֵשׁ לָהֶם שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא קְלָפִים בְּבֵית הֶמְסֵס שֶׁלּוֹ, פַּעַם אַחַת נָפַל אֶרֶז אֶחָד שֶׁבִּמְקוֹמֵנוּ, וְעָבְרוּ שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה קְרוֹנוֹת עַל חוּדּוֹ אַחַת.

b5.he: פַּעַם אַחַת נָפְלָה בֵּיצַת בַּר יוֹכָנִי, וְטִבְּעָה שִׁשִּׁים כְּרַכִּים, וְשִׁבְּרָה שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת אֲרָזִים. וּמִי שָׁדְיָא לֵיהּ? וְהָא כְּתִיב: ״כְּנַף רְנָנִים נֶעֱלָסָה״! אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָהוּא מוּזַרְתָּא הֲוַאי.

b6.he: מַתְנִי׳ שָׁלֹשׁ גֳּרָנוֹת לְמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה: בִּפְרַס הַפֶּסַח, וּבִפְרַס הָעֲצֶרֶת, וּבִפְרַס הֶחָג, וְהֵן גֳּרָנוֹת שֶׁל מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.

b7.he: בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בַּאֲדָר, בְּאֶחָד בְּסִיוָן, בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב. רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים: בְּאֶחָד בְּנִיסָן, בְּאֶחָד בְּסִיוָן, בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בֶּאֱלוּל. וְלָמָה אָמְרוּ בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בֶּאֱלוּל וְלֹא אָמְרוּ בְּאֶחָד בְּתִשְׁרִי? מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא יוֹם טוֹב, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְעַשֵּׂר בְּיוֹם טוֹב — לְפִיכָךְ הִקְדִּימוּהוּ בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בֶּאֱלוּל.

b8.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: בְּאֶחָד בֶּאֱלוּל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לְמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה. בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר: הָאֱלוּלִים מִתְעַשְּׂרִים בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן.

b9.he: כׇּל הַנּוֹלָדִים מֵאֶחָד בְּתִשְׁרִי עַד עֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בֶּאֱלוּל — הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מִצְטָרְפִין. חֲמִשָּׁה לִפְנֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה לְאַחַר רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה — אֵינָן מִצְטָרְפִין. חֲמִשָּׁה לִפְנֵי הַגּוֹרֶן וַחֲמִשָּׁה לְאַחַר הַגּוֹרֶן — הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מִצְטָרְפִין. אִם כֵּן, לָמָּה נֶאֶמְרוּ שָׁלֹשׁ גֳּרָנוֹת לְמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה? שֶׁעַד שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ הַגּוֹרֶן — מוּתָּר לִמְכּוֹר וְלִשְׁחוֹט, הִגִּיעַ הַגּוֹרֶן — לֹא יִשְׁחוֹט, וְאִם שָׁחַט — פָּטוּר.

b10.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי שְׁנָא תְּלָת? אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא: לָקֳבֵל חוּרְפֵי, וְאַפְלֵי, וְקַיְיטֵי.

b11.he: וּמַאי שְׁנָא בְּהָנֵי זִימְנֵי? אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִיָּיא אִישׁ כְּפַר עַכּוֹ:

messages.text: Continued from 56b: brothers who divided their father’s flock and then joined as partners again. Rabbi Elazar said they are exempt from animal tithe only if the division was nine large goats for ten kids; Rabbi Yoḥanan said that even an even division does not show that each share was his from the outset.
And Rabbi Yoḥanan follows his established line of reasoning in this regard.

notes.he: דאין ברירה:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yoḥanan follows his line of reasoning: that there is no retroactive designation [ein bereira].

notes.he: ואע"ג דהכא פליג ר"א עליה דרבי יוחנן ולעיל בסוף יש בכור (בכורות דף כב:) משמע דמודה בההיא דלקוחות הן ומשני מאי אין חוזרין לבטלה הא מצריכין הכא תרי מילי דר' יוחנן א"נ לעיל איצטריך לשנויי דלא תקשי מיניה עליה דרבי יוחנן:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yoḥanan follows his line of reasoning, etc.: Here Rabbi Elazar disagrees with Rabbi Yoḥanan, while above, at the end of Yesh Bekhor [52b; the printed reference reads 22b], it is implied that he concedes in that case that they are purchasers, where the Gemara answers: what does “they do not return” mean? They do not return for nothing [i.e., without payment]. This is no contradiction, since here the Gemara treats Rabbi Yoḥanan’s two statements as each necessary [so one may agree about the field and still disagree about tithe]. Alternatively, the answer above was needed only so that that source would not be a difficulty against Rabbi Yoḥanan.

messages.text: The English translation reads “as Rav Asi says” here; the Aramaic reads Rabbi Asi, Rabbi Yoḥanan’s student, who reports the same ruling on 52b.

Brothers who divided real estate received as an inheritance are considered purchasers who have purchased from each other, and as purchasers of land they must return the portions to each other in the Jubilee Year, at which point they may redistribute the property.

notes.he: דלית ליה ברירה ומשום הכי מחזירין זה לזה ביובל דאין אומרין זהו חלקו המגיעו:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yoḥanan follows his line of reasoning: he does not accept retroactive designation, and therefore they return [the portions] to each other in the Jubilee, since we do not say: this is the portion that was his due.

messages.text: This demonstrates that Rabbi Yoḥanan does not hold that it is retroactively established that each brother’s portion was designated for him upon their father’s death. Rather, it is considered as though all the land was joint property until the brothers traded or bought their respective portions from each other.
And both statements of Rabbi Yoḥanan are necessary.
messages.quote: Brothers who divided real estate received as an inheritance are considered purchasers

notes.he: הנך תרתי דרבי יוחנן:
notes.en: And they are necessary: these two statements of Rabbi Yoḥanan.

messages.text: As, if he had taught this halakha to us only here, with regard to animal tithe, one might have thought that it is in this case that Rabbi Yoḥanan says each one has not received his own portion. This is because the case must be similar to the case of your firstborn son, in accordance with the juxtaposition between the two cases. Just as your firstborn son is redeemed only if it is clear to you that he is your son, not if he is purchased from another, so too, your cattle and your sheep are subject to animal tithe only if it is clear to you, i.e., if there is no aspect of acquisition at all.

notes.he: דאין ברירה ופטורין משום דמעשר בהמה איתקש לבנך כדכתיב (שמות כ״ב:כ״ח-כ״ט) בכור בניך תתן לי כן תעשה וגו':
notes.en: In this case Rabbi Yoḥanan says: that there is no retroactive designation and they are exempt, because animal tithe is juxtaposed to “your son,” as it is written (Exodus 22:28–29): “The firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me; so shall you do [with your oxen and with your sheep].”

notes.he: שנולד ברשותך:
notes.en: When it is clear to you: that it was born in your possession.

notes.he: שיהא חלקך ואין ברירה. אבל שדה של ירושה דלאו מכר הוא אימא לא ליהדר:
notes.en: So too your cattle and your sheep, when it is clear to you: that it is your own share, and there is no retroactive designation. But an inherited field, which is not a sale, I might say need not be returned.

messages.text: But in the case of a field, one might think it is only with regard to a field that is sold that the Merciful One states that the purchaser should return it in the Jubilee Year, whereas a field that is an inheritance or a gift need not be returned.

And if Rabbi Yoḥanan had taught us only the halakha that a field inherited by two brothers must be returned in the Jubilee Year, one might have thought that Rabbi Yoḥanan was uncertain and therefore ruled to be stringent. If so, he would rule stringently with regard to animal tithe as well, deeming the brothers liable.

notes.he: הוה אמינא בההיא קאמר רבי יוחנן משום דלחומרא אזיל משום ספיקא אבל הכא דלקולא הוא דמיפטר ממעשר אי נמי לכתחלה דלגבי יובל בעינן שתהא חוזרת קרקע לתחלתה שהיתה ביחד אבל גבי מעשר ליכא למימר הכי:
notes.en: And if he had taught us the field: I would have said that it is there that Rabbi Yoḥanan says this, because he goes toward stringency on account of the uncertainty; but here it would be a leniency, since they would be exempt from tithe. Alternatively, “at the beginning”: with the Jubilee we require the land to return to its beginning, when it was held together; but with tithe one cannot say this.

notes.he: ירושה דמחזירין זה לזה דכלקוחות הן היינו חומרא. אבל הכא גבי מעשר בהמה אי משוינן לה כלקוחות היינו קולא דפטירי ממעשר אימא לא:
notes.en: And if he had taught us the field: an inheritance, which they return to each other because they are like purchasers, that is a stringency. But here, with animal tithe, if we treat them as purchasers that is a leniency, since they are exempt from tithe; I might say not.

messages.text: Alternatively, one might think Rabbi Yoḥanan rules in this manner with regard to returning fields in the Jubilee Year only because the field must return to how it was in the beginning. But here, in the case of animal tithe, where there is no requirement to return matters to their initial state, one might say that the brothers are not considered to be purchasers, but rather each received the animals that were retroactively designated for him and they are therefore obligated in animal tithe. For this reason it is necessary for Rabbi Yoḥanan to teach both cases.

notes.he: דכלקוחות הן ומחזירין משום דכתחילה כלומר דהשתא כי מחזירין שייך כל חד וחד לדחבריה כבתחלה. כמעיקרא קודם חלוקה ומקיימי קרא דכתיב תשובו איש לאחוזתו הילכך קאמר אין ברירה כי היכי דמחזירין אבל הכא מעשר בהמה דלית ביה דין חזרה ביובל אימא ליהוי ברירה קמ"ל דלא:
notes.en: Alternatively: had he taught us about a field that they are like purchasers and return it, that would be because of “at the beginning”: that is, now when they return [the portions], each one’s share goes back to the other as at the beginning, as it was before the division, and they fulfil the verse “you shall return every man to his possession.” That is why he says there is no retroactive designation, so that they return. But here, with animal tithe, which has no law of return in the Jubilee, I might say there is retroactive designation. It teaches us that there is not.

messages.text: The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita against the opinion that there is retroactive designation of the animals.

And similarly in the case of two partners who divided their common property, and one took ten lambs and the other one took nine lambs and a dog, sacrificing any of the ten lambs taken in exchange for the dog is prohibited. This is because they are considered “the price of a dog,” as it states in the Torah, since they were given in exchange for it. Nevertheless, the nine lambs that were taken with the dog are permitted for sacrifice.

verse.he: לֹא־תָבִיא אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה וּמְחִיר כֶּלֶב בֵּית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְכׇל־נֶדֶר כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ גַּם־שְׁנֵיהֶם׃ {ס}
verse.en: You shall not bring the fee of a whore or the pay of a dog into the house of the ETERNAL your God in fulfillment of any vow, for both are abhorrent to the ETERNAL your God.

notes.he: במסכת תמורה בפרק כל האסורין:
notes.en: And similarly partners: [this is taught] in Tractate Temura, in the chapter Kol HaAsurin.

notes.dh: אחד נטל עשרה טלאים ואחד תשעה טלאים וכלב
notes.he: עמהן אותן עשרה הטלאים שכנגד הכלב אסורין למזבח דאחד מהן היה חילופו של כלב והיה מחיר כלב ולא ידעינן הי ניהו:
notes.en: One took ten lambs and one took nine lambs and a dog with them: those ten lambs opposite the dog are forbidden for the altar, since one of them was the dog’s exchange and so is “the price of a dog,” and we do not know which one it is.

notes.he: התשעה שעם הכלב לית בהו איסורא:
notes.en: Those with the dog: the nine with the dog have no prohibition in them.

messages.text: And if you say that there is retroactive designation, why are all ten lambs prohibited? Let him select one of the lambs to correspond to the dog and take it away, and all the rest of these lambs should be permitted.
messages.quote: sacrificing any of the ten lambs taken in exchange for the dog is prohibited

notes.dh: לברור חד מיניהו להדי כלב כו'
notes.he: וא"ת מה יועיל הא אין ידוע איזהו אותו שכנגד הכלב וכי תימא לפי ששוה לכלב הא דאמר אי דשוו כולהו להדדי ה"נ ואז היאך יכול לברר אותו שכנגד הכלב להתיר האחרים וי"ל שכך סברת הש"ס כיון שיש ברירה שיש לדבר להיות תלוי בדעתו דמסתמא כך דעתו מתחלה דאותו שיברור הוא כנגד הכלב:
notes.en: Let him select one of them to correspond to the dog, etc.: And if you ask, what would that help? It is not known which one is opposite the dog. And if you say, the one that is worth as much as the dog: but [Rav Ashi] says, “if they are all equal to each other, indeed” [one may select], and then how can he pick out the one opposite the dog so as to permit the others? One may answer that this is the Gemara’s reasoning: since there is retroactive designation, the matter can depend on his intent, for presumably his intent from the start was that the one he will select is the one opposite the dog.

messages.text: If this is referring to a case where they are all equal in value to each other, indeed one may consider only one of the lambs as corresponding to the dog.
messages.quote: Let him select one of the lambs to correspond to the dog

notes.he: שכל כבש שבאותן תשעה יש לו חבר באותן העשרה ששוה כמותו ונמצא שהעשירי כנגד הכלב הכי נמי דיש ברירה ונוטל אחד במחיר כלב ואוכלו והשאר מותרין לגבוה:
notes.en: If they are all equal to each other: every lamb among those nine has a counterpart among the ten worth the same, so the tenth turns out to be opposite the dog. Indeed, there is retroactive designation: he takes one as the price of the dog and eats it, and the rest are permitted for the Most High [the altar].

notes.he: כל העשרה דלא ידעינן הי ניהו הוי מחיר כלב חילופו. אי דשוו כולהי עשרה כהדדי כל חד וחד שוה כמו הכלב הכי נמי דאמרינן ליברר חד כנגד הכלב:
notes.en: Those opposite the dog are forbidden: all ten, since we do not know which is the price of the dog, its exchange. If all ten are equal to each other, each one worth as much as the dog, indeed we say: let him select one opposite the dog.

messages.text: Here, we are dealing with a case where they are not all equal in value to each other, but the value of this dog is one and a small amount more than the value of each one of the ten lambs. Therefore, one cannot set aside a single lamb in exchange for the dog, and consequently one draws this extra small amount, i.e., the additional value of the dog, and divides it between all of the other nine lambs. As a result, all ten lambs are prohibited, since part of the price of a dog is included in each of them.

notes.he: דכולהו אסירי כגון דלא שוו אהדדי שתשעה כבשים שבתוך עשרה שוין יותר מתשעה שעם אותו הכלב והכלב שוה את העשירי ואותו משהו ששוין אותן תשעה שכנגדן יותר מתשעה שעמו דהשתא הוי מחיר כלב הולך בכל התשעה שכנגדו בכל חד פורתא והעשירי כנגדו. והמורה גריס כגון דשוה כל חד וחד ארבעה זוזי ופלגי חומשא וכלבא חמשא זוזי דההוא זוזא שייך ואתי בכולהו ופירושא הכי דשוי כל חד וחד מאותן עשרה שכנגד הכלב ד' זוזי ופלגי חומשא דזוזא נמצא שכל העשרה שוין ארבעים וחד זוזי שעשרה חצאי חומשין עושין ה' חומשין דהיינו זוזא והכלב שוה ה' זוזים נמצא שתשעה שעמו אינן אלא נ"ו זוז ואיהו חמשא הרי ארבעין וחד השתא לא שוו אותן שעם הכלב אלא ד' זוזי כל חד ואותן שכנגדו שוו כל חד ד' זוזי ופלגא חומשא דזוזא נמצא שהכלב משוה את כולם ובכל אותן שכנגדו שייך חילוף הכלב אותו חצי חומש שכל אחד שוה יותר על ארבע זוז מחילוף שכנגד אותו זוז שהכלב שוה יותר מארבע:
notes.en: Here we are dealing with a case where all of them are forbidden, for example where they are not equal to each other: the nine lambs among the ten are worth more than the nine with the dog, and the dog is worth the tenth plus that small amount by which those nine opposite exceed the nine with it. Now the price of the dog runs through all nine opposite it, a little in each, and the tenth is opposite it. And the Teacher reads: for example, where each one is worth four zuz and half a fifth, and the dog five zuz, that one zuz is shared and runs into all of them. The explanation is this: each of the ten opposite the dog is worth four zuz and half a fifth of a zuz, so all ten are worth forty-one zuz, since ten halves of a fifth make five fifths, which is one zuz. The dog is worth five zuz, so the nine with it come to only thirty-six zuz [the printed text reads fifty-six], and with the dog’s five that makes forty-one. Now those with the dog are worth only four zuz each, and those opposite it four zuz and half a fifth each; the dog evens them all out, and the dog’s exchange is shared among all those opposite it: the half-fifth by which each is worth more than four zuz, against the one zuz by which the dog is worth more than four.

notes.he: וליכא ברירה הלכך שכנגד הכלב כולן אסורין להקרבה:
notes.en: For this small amount is shared among all ten, and there is no retroactive designation; therefore all those opposite the dog are forbidden for sacrifice.

messages.text: Mishna

All cattle, sheep, and goats enter the pen to be tithed, except for an animal crossbred from diverse kinds, e.g., a hybrid of a goat and a sheep; a tereifa; an animal born by caesarean section; one whose time has not yet arrived, i.e., that is younger than eight days old, which is when animals become eligible for sacrifice; and an orphan.

notes.he: הוה מצי נמי למיתני נדמה דהא מפרש טעמא בגמרא משום דילפינן תחת תחת מקדשים אבל בכל מקום דחשיב (טרפה) רגיל לדלג נדמה כאילו הוא בכלל כלאים משום דדמי ליה קצת:
notes.en: Except for diverse kinds, etc.: It could also have listed an animal that resembles [another kind], since the Gemara explains the reason as being that we derive “under,” “under” from consecrated animals. But everywhere it lists [these], it usually skips the resembling animal, as though it were included in diverse kinds, since it is somewhat like it.

messages.text: And what is an orphan? It is any animal whose mother died or was slaughtered while giving birth to it and thereafter completed giving birth to it.

notes.he: בשעת לידה. וכל טעמא דמתניתין מפרש בגמרא:
notes.en: Mishna. Any whose mother died: at the time of birth. The whole reasoning of the mishna is explained in the Gemara.

notes.he: כשנולד זה או נשחטה שזה פירש למיתה וזה לחיים:
notes.en: Any whose mother died: when this one was born, or was slaughtered; for the one [the mother] departs toward death and this one toward life.

messages.text: Even if its mother was slaughtered but its hide exists at birth, i.e., if the mother’s hide is present after the birth, this is not an orphan.

notes.he: והעור קיים:
notes.en: And the shelaḥ exists: and the hide exists.

notes.he: בגמרא מפרש טעמא:
notes.en: This is not an orphan: the Gemara explains the reason.

notes.he: העור שלה שיכול אדם לכורכו בעור אמו ולחממו בו אין זה יתום:
notes.en: And the shelaḥ exists: her hide, so that one can wrap it in its mother’s hide and warm it with it; this is not an orphan.

messages.text: Gemara
From where are these matters, i.e., the fact that those animals are not included in the animal tithe, derived? As the Sages taught in a baraita that discusses offerings in general:
messages.quote: except for an animal crossbred from diverse kinds

messages.text: “When a bull or a sheep or a goat is born, then it shall be seven days under its mother, but from the eighth day onward it may be accepted for an offering made by fire to the Lord.” The phrase “a bull or a sheep” serves to exclude an animal born from diverse kinds; “or a goat” serves to exclude an animal that resembles another, e.g., a sheep that is the offspring of two sheep but which looks like a goat, or vice versa; “when…is born” serves to exclude an animal born by caesarean section; “then it shall be seven days” serves to exclude an animal whose time has not yet arrived; “under its mother” serves to exclude an orphan.

verse.he: שׁוֹר אוֹ־כֶשֶׂב אוֹ־עֵז כִּי יִוָּלֵד וְהָיָה שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תַּחַת אִמּוֹ וּמִיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי וָהָלְאָה יֵרָצֶה לְקׇרְבַּן אִשֶּׁה לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: When an ox or a sheep or a goat is born, it shall stay seven days with its mother, and from the eighth day on it shall be acceptable as an offering by fire to GOD.

notes.he: גבי שאר כל הקדשים כתיב:
notes.en: A bull or a sheep: this is written about all the other consecrated animals.

notes.he: שאמו רחל והוא דומה לעז:
notes.en: Resembling: whose mother is a ewe and it looks like a goat.

notes.he: מן התייש והרחל בא:
notes.en: Diverse kinds: it comes from a he-goat and a ewe.

notes.he: שיהא מיוחד שור או כשב פרט לכלאים:
notes.en: A bull or a sheep: it must be distinctly a bull or a sheep; this excludes diverse kinds.

messages.text: It is learned by a verbal analogy from the term “under.” It is stated here, with regard to animal tithe: “Whatever passes under the rod,” and it is stated there, with regard to all offerings: “Under its mother.” Just as there, in the case of all offerings, the verse serves to exclude all these categories, so too here, with regard to animal tithe, the verse serves to exclude all these categories.
messages.lead: The baraita continues: From where is it derived that these halakhot also apply to animal tithe?

verse.he: וְכׇל־מַעְשַׂר בָּקָר וָצֹאן כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲבֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט הָעֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: All tithes of the herd or flock—of all that passes under the shepherd’s staff, every tenth one—shall be holy to GOD.

notes.he: במעשר בהמה תחת השבט:
notes.en: It is stated here: with animal tithe, “under the rod.”

notes.he: בכל הקדשים תחת אמו:
notes.en: And it is stated there: with all consecrated animals, “under its mother.”

notes.he: בכל הקדשים:
notes.en: Just as there: with all consecrated animals.

notes.he: כדפרישית כלאים ונדמה ויוצא דופן ומחוסר זמן ויתום אף במעשר הכי נמי והיינו טעמא דמתניתין ומה מעשר פרט לטרפה דכתיב בה (ויקרא כז) כל אשר יעבור פרט לטרפה שאינה עוברת דבהמה שנחתכו רגליה מן הארכובה ולמעלה זו היא אחת מי"ח טריפות:
notes.en: Excluding all these categories: as I explained, diverse kinds, the resembling animal, one born by caesarean section, one whose time has not arrived, and an orphan; so too with tithe. And that is the reason of the mishna. And just as tithe excludes a tereifa, as it is written of it (Leviticus 27:32), “whatever passes,” excluding a tereifa, which does not pass: an animal whose legs were cut off from the knee [arkhuba] upward, which is one of the eighteen tereifot.

messages.text: And just as here, with regard to animal tithe, the verse serves to exclude a tereifa, as the verse states: “Whatever passes under the rod,” and a tereifa is unable to pass unaided, so too there, with regard to all offerings, the verse serves to exclude a tereifa.

notes.he: ומה כאן במעשר פרט לטרפה (שבגלוי) דכתיב כל אשר יעבור פרט לטרפה שאינה עוברת אף להלן בקדשים פרט לטרפה:
notes.en: And just as here, with tithe, it excludes a tereifa, as it is written “whatever passes,” excluding a tereifa that does not pass, so too there, with consecrated animals, it excludes a tereifa.

messages.text: What does the mishna’s expansive term: All, serve to include? It serves to include this halakha that the Sages taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: All cattle, sheep, and goats enter the pen to be tithed

notes.he: דקתני במתניתין לאיתויי מאי:
notes.en: All: which is taught in the mishna; what does it come to include?

messages.text: With regard to an animal that copulated with a person, or an animal that was the object of bestiality, or an animal that was set aside for idol worship, or one that was worshipped as a deity, or one that was given as payment to a prostitute or as the price of a dog, or a tumtum, i.e., an animal whose sexual organs are indeterminate, or a hermaphrodite, i.e., an animal displaying sexual organs of both sexes, all of these enter the pen to be tithed despite the fact that they are disqualified from being brought as offerings.

notes.he: שהפרישוהו להקריבו לעבודה זרה:
notes.en: Set aside [mukẓe]: one that they set aside to offer to idol worship.

notes.he: שעבד את הבהמה עצמה כגון שניסך לה בין קרניה:
notes.en: Worshipped: one where he worshipped the animal itself, for example he poured a libation to it between its horns.

messages.text: A tumtum and a hermaphrodite do not enter the pen to be tithed.

notes.he: דקסבר דבריה היא:
notes.en: A tumtum does not enter: since he holds that it is a creature of its own kind.

messages.text: But as for the tanna of our mishna, if he derives the verbal analogy of: “Under,” and: “Under,” from the verse referring to sacrificial animals, then these types listed in the baraita should also not enter the pen to be tithed, as they are all disqualified from being sacrificed.
messages.quote: all of these enter the pen to be tithed

notes.he: תנא דמתניתין דתנא הכל לאתויי כל הני דמתניתין:
notes.en: And our tanna: the tanna of the mishna, who teaches “all” to include all these [listed in the baraita].

notes.he: מעשר תחת תחת מקדשים:
notes.en: If he derives: tithe from consecrated animals, through “under,” “under.”

notes.he: דהא כולהו פסולי בקדשים דתניא בתמורה בפרק כל האסורין (תמורה דף כח.) מן הבהמה להוציא רובע ונרבע וכגון שאין בדבר אלא עד אחד דאי שני עדים בת קטלא היא דכתיב ואת הבהמה תהרוגו מן הבקר להוציא את הנעבד מן הצאן להוציא את המוקצה:
notes.en: These too should not [enter]: for all of them are disqualified as offerings, as is taught in Temura, in the chapter Kol HaAsurin (Temura 28a): “from the cattle” excludes the animal that copulated with a person and the one that was the object of bestiality, where there is only one witness to the matter, for with two witnesses it is liable to death, as it is written, “and you shall kill the animal”; “from the herd” excludes the worshipped animal; “from the flock” excludes the one set aside.

messages.text: And if he does not derive the verbal analogy from sacrificial animals, from where does he derive the exemption of these categories listed in the mishna, e.g., one whose time has not yet arrived and an orphan?

notes.he: מקדשים הני אחריני מחוסר זמן ויתום מנא ליה דאין מעשרין:
notes.en: And if he does not derive: from consecrated animals, then these others, one whose time has not arrived and an orphan, from where does he know that they are not tithed?

notes.he: הנך גופייהו דממעט מנא ליה:
notes.en: And if he does not derive: these very ones that he excludes, from where does he know them?

messages.text: Actually, the tanna does derive the verbal analogy, but these categories listed in the baraita are included by the Merciful One in the animal tithe. As it is written with regard to those animals that may not be brought as offerings: “Neither from the hand of a foreigner shall you offer the bread of your God of any of these, because their corruption is in them, there is a blemish in them.” This verse indicates that corruption is considered a blemish,

verse.he: וּמִיַּד בֶּן־נֵכָר לֹא תַקְרִיבוּ אֶת־לֶחֶם אֱלֹהֵיכֶם מִכׇּל־אֵלֶּה כִּי מׇשְׁחָתָם בָּהֶם מוּם בָּם לֹא יֵרָצוּ לָכֶם׃ {ס}
verse.en: nor shall you accept such [animals] from a foreigner for offering as food for your God, for they are mutilated, they have a defect; they shall not be accepted in your favor.

notes.he: רובע ונרבע וכולהו אינך רחמנא רבינהו דלעשרי ואף על גב דלא חזו להקרבה יאכלו במומן לבעלים:
notes.en: And these: the animal that copulated, the one that was the object, and all the rest. The Merciful One included them to be tithed, and even though they are unfit to be sacrificed, they are eaten by their owners with their blemish.

messages.text: Anywhere that the term: Corruption, is stated, it is a reference to nothing other than a matter of licentiousness and idol worship.
messages.lead: and the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:

messages.text: Corruption is a reference to a matter of licentiousness, as it is written with regard to the generation of the flood: “And God saw the earth, and behold, it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted their way upon the earth.”

verse.he: וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת־הָאָרֶץ וְהִנֵּה נִשְׁחָתָה כִּי־הִשְׁחִית כׇּל־בָּשָׂר אֶת־דַּרְכּוֹ עַל־הָאָרֶץ׃ {ס}
verse.en: When God saw how corrupt the earth was, for all flesh had corrupted its ways on earth,

messages.text: And corruption is also a reference to idol worship, as it is written: “Lest you deal corruptly, and make you a graven image, the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female.”

verse.he: פֶּן־תַּשְׁחִתוּן וַעֲשִׂיתֶם לָכֶם פֶּסֶל תְּמוּנַת כׇּל־סָמֶל תַּבְנִית זָכָר אוֹ נְקֵבָה׃
verse.en: not to act wickedly and make for yourselves a sculptured image in any likeness whatever: the form of a man or a woman,

messages.text: And the juxtaposition of the word “corruption” with the word “blemish” teaches that in any case where a blemish disqualifies an animal, a matter of licentiousness or a matter of idol worship also disqualifies it. And in a case where a blemish does not disqualify an animal, a matter of licentiousness or a matter of idol worship also does not disqualify it.

notes.dh: כל שהמום פוסל בו דבר ערוה ועבודה זרה פוסלין בו
notes.he: דהא אקשינהו רחמנא למום דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ב:כ״ה) כי משחתם בהם מום בם:
notes.en: Wherever a blemish disqualifies, licentiousness and idol worship disqualify: for the Merciful One juxtaposed them to a blemish, as it is written (Leviticus 22:25): “because their corruption is in them, there is a blemish in them.”

notes.dh: כל שהמום פוסל בו דבר ערוה ועבודה זרה פוסלין בו
notes.he: כולי עלמא אית להו הך דרשא אפי' מאן דממעט רובע ונרבע מוקצה ונעבד ממן הבהמה וממן הבקר בפ' כל האסורין (תמורה כח.) כדפירשתי (לעיל בפרק הלוקח בהמה):
notes.en: Wherever a blemish disqualifies, licentiousness and idol worship disqualify: everyone accepts this exposition, even the one who excludes the animal that copulated, the one that was the object of bestiality, the one set aside and the one worshipped from “from the cattle” and “from the herd” in the chapter Kol HaAsurin (Temura 28a), as I explained above in the chapter HaLokeaḥ Behema.

messages.text: And with regard to this animal tithe, since a blemish on an animal does not disqualify it, as it is written: “He shall not inquire whether it be good or bad, neither shall he change it,” a matter of licentiousness or a matter of idol worship also does not disqualify it.

verse.he: לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין־טוֹב לָרַע וְלֹא יְמִירֶנּוּ וְאִם־הָמֵר יְמִירֶנּוּ וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לֹא יִגָּאֵל׃
verse.en: One must not look out for good as against bad, or make substitution for it. If one does make substitution for it, then it and its substitute shall both be holy: it cannot be redeemed.

messages.text: The categories listed in the baraita are either matters of licentiousness or matters of idol worship. An animal that copulated with a person and an animal that was the object of bestiality are both a matter of licentiousness. An animal that was set aside for idol worship and one that was worshipped are cases of idol worship. And an animal that was given as payment to a prostitute is a matter of licentiousness, and an animal used as the price of a dog is juxtaposed to an animal that was given as payment to a prostitute (see Deuteronomy 23:19).

notes.he: דכתיב בחד קרא:
notes.en: Is juxtaposed: [the price of a dog] is not taught [as licentiousness itself; it is juxtaposed to the payment to a prostitute] because they are written in one verse.

messages.text: Finally, with regard to an animal that is a tumtum or a hermaphrodite, the tanna holds that it is uncertain whether it is male or female, not a creature unto itself, and therefore a tumtum is also subject to the tithe.

notes.he: אי זכר אי נקבה הלכך ממה נפשך מיעשרי ורבי שמעון סבר בריה בפני עצמה היא:
notes.en: A tumtum and a hermaphrodite, it is uncertain: whether it is male or female; therefore, whichever it is, they are tithed. And Rabbi Shimon holds that it is a creature of its own kind.

notes.he: וממה נפשך אי זכר הוא אי נקבה היא חייב במעשר:
notes.en: He holds it is uncertain: and whichever way, whether it is male or female, it is obligated in tithe.

messages.text: The baraita states that Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon: A tumtum and a hermaphrodite do not enter the pen to be tithed. He holds that the case of an animal that is a tumtum or a hermaphrodite involves an uncertainty, and the Merciful One excluded cases of uncertainty with regard to sacrificial animals. Only a definite male or a definite female is fit to be sacrificed on the altar, but not a tumtum or a hermaphrodite. Consequently, with regard to animal tithe too, they do not enter the pen to be tithed, as he derives the verbal analogy of “under” and “under” from sacrificial animals.
messages.quote: A tumtum and a hermaphrodite do not enter the pen to be tithed

notes.dh: זכר ודאי נקבה ודאית לא טומטום כו'
notes.he: הך סוגיא דלא כרב חסדא וריש לקיש כדפרישית לעיל בסוף על אלו מומין (בכורות דף מב:):
notes.en: A definite male, a definite female, but not a tumtum, etc.: this passage does not follow Rav Ḥisda and Reish Lakish, as I explained above at the end of Al Elu Mumin (Bekhorot 42b).

messages.text: The Sages taught in a baraita:

All animals enter the pen to be tithed except for an animal crossbred from diverse kinds, e.g., a hybrid of a goat and a sheep, and a tereifa; this is the statement of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yehuda, of the village of Bartota, who said it in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua.

I heard from Rabbi Yehoshua that an animal born by caesarean section and an animal whose time has not yet arrived, i.e., that is less than eight days old, and an orphan animal, are also excluded from animal tithe.

And the first tanna of the baraita, what does he maintain? If he derives the verbal analogy of “under” and “under” from sacrificial animals, then these categories listed by Rabbi Akiva should also not enter the pen to be tithed.
messages.quote: except for an animal crossbred from diverse kinds, and a tereifa

notes.he: יוצא דופן ומחוסר זמן ויתום:
notes.en: These too should not: one born by caesarean section, one whose time has not arrived, and an orphan.

messages.text: And if he does not derive the verbal analogy, granted, he rules that a tereifa does not enter the pen to be tithed, as it is written: “Whatever passes under the rod,” which excludes a tereifa, as it does not pass under the rod due to its physical state. But from where does he derive that an animal crossbred from diverse kinds does not enter the pen to be tithed?

verse.he: וְכׇל־מַעְשַׂר בָּקָר וָצֹאן כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲבֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט הָעֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: All tithes of the herd or flock—of all that passes under the shepherd’s staff, every tenth one—shall be holy to GOD.

notes.he: דבהמה שנחתכו רגליה מן הארכובה ולמעלה היא מי"ח טרפות והתם במנחות (דף ו.) מצריך תלתא קראי בטרפה חד לטרפה ממעי אמו דלא היתה לה שעת הכושר וחד לטרפה ואחר כך הקדישה וחד להקדישה ואחר כך נטרפה ומן הארכובה ולמטה חשבינן ליה עוברת כיון דאינה נטרפה:
notes.en: Excluding a tereifa, which does not pass: for an animal whose legs were cut off from the knee upward is one of the eighteen tereifot. And there, in Menaḥot (6a), three verses are needed for a tereifa: one for an animal that was a tereifa from its mother’s womb, which never had a time of fitness; one for an animal that became a tereifa and was afterward consecrated; and one for an animal that was consecrated and afterward became a tereifa. An animal cut from the knee downward we count as one that passes, since it is not a tereifa.

messages.text: Actually, he does derive the verbal analogy of “under” and “under,” and therefore he excludes a tereifa and diverse kinds from the animal tithe. But with regard to an animal born by caesarean section

he holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, who says that a human child born by caesarean section is a full-fledged offspring and renders its mother ritually impure with the impurity of childbirth. Likewise, with regard to an animal born by caesarean section, he holds the birth was a proper birth and the animal may be brought as an offering, and therefore it also enters the pen to be tithed.

notes.he: במסכת נדה בפרק יוצא דופן (נדה דף מ.) קא"ר שמעון דהרי זה כילוד ואמו טמאה לידה וריש לקיש מפרש טעמא בגמרא תלד לרבות יוצא דופן והכי נמי אמרינן כי יולד לרבות יוצא דופן:
notes.en: Is a full-fledged offspring: in Tractate Nidda, in the chapter Yotzei Dofen (Nidda 40a), Rabbi Shimon says that it counts as born and its mother is impure with the impurity of childbirth, and Reish Lakish explains the reason there in the Gemara: “she shall bear” includes one born by caesarean section. So here too we say: “when it is born” includes one born by caesarean section.

notes.he: ביוצא דופן סבר לה כר' שמעון דאמר במס' נדה ולד מעליא הוא דכתיב אם נקבה תלד לרבות יוצא דופן:
notes.en: With regard to one born by caesarean section, he holds like Rabbi Shimon, who says in Tractate Nidda that it is a full-fledged offspring, as it is written, “and if she bears a female,” to include one born by caesarean section.

messages.text: And this is not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan, who holds that Rabbi Shimon concedes that an animal born by caesarean section is disqualified from being brought as an offering (see Nidda 40a).

notes.he: דאמר התם בההוא פירקא דמודה ר"ש לעניין קדשים שאינו קדוש דגמר לידה לידה מבכור דבעי רחם:
notes.en: And not in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan: who says there, in that same chapter, that Rabbi Shimon concedes with regard to consecrated animals that it is not sanctified, since he derives “birth,” “birth” from the firstborn, which requires [the opening of] the womb.

notes.he: דפליג עליה התם דאמר מודי ר' שמעון לענין קדשים שאינו קדוש דלא הוי ולד:
notes.en: And not in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan: who disagrees with him there and says that Rabbi Shimon concedes with regard to consecrated animals that it is not sanctified, since it is not an offspring.

messages.text: And with regard to an animal whose time has not yet arrived, this tanna holds in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda, who maintains that the obligation of animal tithe applies to such an animal.

notes.he: דאמר דנכנס לדיר להתעשר וכדפרשינן למילתיה לעיל בפרק הלוקח בהמה מן העובד כוכבים (בכורות דף כא:):
notes.en: Like Rabbi Shimon [so Rashi’s heading; the printed Gemara reads Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda]: who says that it enters the pen to be tithed, as we explained his statement above in the chapter HaLokeaḥ Behema Min HaOved Kokhavim (Bekhorot 21b).

notes.dh: במחוסר זמן סבר לה כר' שמעון בן יהודה
notes.he: דאמר לעיל מחוסר זמן נכנס לדיר להתעשר והרי הוא כבכור כו':
notes.en: With regard to one whose time has not arrived, he holds like Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda, who said above that one whose time has not arrived enters the pen to be tithed, and it is like a firstborn, etc.

messages.text: As for an orphan animal, he is referring to a case where the mother’s hide exists at birth, i.e., the mother’s hide is present after the birth, and therefore the animal is not considered an orphan. And Rabbi Yehoshua, whose opinion this tanna follows, conforms to his standard line of reasoning, as he says: Even if its mother was slaughtered but its hide exists at birth, i.e., if the mother’s hide is present after the birth, this is not an orphan.
messages.quote: Even if its mother was slaughtered but its hide exists … this is not an orphan

notes.he: והעור קיים כשיצא הולד לחוץ:
notes.en: And the shelaḥ: and the hide exists when the offspring comes out.

messages.text: In our locale, if an animal dies while giving birth they flay the dead mother’s skin and clothe the living newborn animal with it for protection.

notes.he: מקום:
notes.en: Ben Satriel of Arkat Leveina: a place.

notes.he: כשמקשה מחמת הוולד מפשיטים עור האם שהיא מתה ומלבישין אותו לולד שהוא חי ומתקיים מפני דבר זה שעושין לו:
notes.en: The dead one: when [the mother] has a hard labor because of the offspring, they flay the hide of the mother, who is dead, and clothe the offspring, which is alive, with it, and it survives because of what they do for it.

notes.he: זהו הולד:
notes.en: The living one: this is the offspring.

notes.he: מערקת לבנה מפשיטין את המתה השלח שלה ומלבישין את החיה היתום:
notes.en: From Arkat Leveina. They flay the dead one, her hide, and clothe the living one, the orphan.

messages.text: @Rabbi Yishmael ben Satriel This testimony of yours reveals the reason for the ruling of the mishna that if the hide of the mother still exists the offspring is not considered to be an orphan; the hide serves as a substitute for the mother.
messages.quote: they flay the dead mother’s skin and clothe the living newborn animal

notes.he: דודאי משום הכי קאמר רבי יהושע אם נולד כל זמן שהעור שהשלח קיים אינו יתום דכיון דהעור מהנה לולד דומה כמי שאמו קיימת:
notes.en: The reason of our mishna is revealed: surely this is why Rabbi Yehoshua says that if it was born while the hide exists it is not an orphan: since the hide benefits the offspring, it is as though its mother were still there.

notes.he: של ר' יהושע וכי עבדי ליה הכי חיי:
notes.en: The reason of our mishna is revealed: that of Rabbi Yehoshua. [A bracketed editorial note proposes reading: surely, since they treat it this way, that is why Rabbi Yehoshua holds so.] And when they do this to it, it lives.

messages.text: The lettuce in our locale has 600,000 leaves in its omasum, i.e., in its core.
messages.lead: He also testified before Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi:

notes.dh: ועוד העיד דבר זה חזירין שבמקומנו
notes.he: לשון חזרת ירק שלועזים לטוג"א:
notes.en: And he further testified this: the ḥazeirin in our locale: a term for ḥazeret, a vegetable (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: היינו אותן עלין קטנים כמו הבשר עצמו שיש באותו המסס של בהמה שקורין צינטול"א:
notes.en: In the beit hamesses: these are the small leaves, like the flesh itself, that are in an animal’s omasum (Rashi adds an Old French gloss).

notes.he: קלפי עלין כקלח אחד:
notes.en: Ḥazeirim: layers of leaves, as on a single stalk.

messages.text: Once one cedar tree fell in our locale, and it was so wide that sixteen wagons passed over its back, meaning the width of its trunk, as one, i.e., side by side.
messages.lead: He further testified before Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi:

notes.dh: ועוד העיד דבר זה פעם אחת כו' על חודו
notes.he: על צידו ברוחבו שהוא עב כל כך שעברו עליו י"ו קרנות זו בצד זו על חודו כלומר ברוחבו של אילן:
notes.en: And he further testified this: once, etc., over its edge: over its side, across its width, which was so thick that sixteen wagons passed over it side by side; “over its edge” means across the width of the tree.

messages.text: Once an egg of the bird called bar yokhani fell, and the contents of the egg drowned sixty cities and broke three hundred cedar trees.
messages.lead: He also testified before Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi:

notes.he: עוף הוא כדאמרינן בכמה דוכתי ואימא כביעא דבר יוכני:
notes.en: Bar yokhani: it is a bird, as we say in several places, “like the egg of the bar yokhani.”

notes.he: ממה שבתוכה:
notes.en: Drowned: with what was inside it.

messages.text: And does the bar yokhani bird throw its eggs to the ground? But isn’t it written: “The kenaf renanim bird rejoices, but are her wings and feathers those of the stork? For she leaves her eggs on the earth, and warms them in dust.” The Sages understood that kenaf renanim is another name for the bar yokhani bird. If so, how could its egg fall if it lays its eggs on the ground?
messages.quote: Once an egg of the bird called bar yokhani fell

verse.he: כְּנַף־רְנָנִים נֶעֱלָסָה אִם־אֶבְרָה חֲסִידָה וְנֹצָה׃ כִּי־תַעֲזֹב לָאָרֶץ בֵּצֶיהָ וְעַל־עָפָר תְּחַמֵּם׃
verse.en:
The wing of the ostrich beats joyously;
Are its pinions and plumage like the stork’s? It leaves its eggs on the ground,
Letting them warm in the dirt,

notes.he: ומתפרש הכי בלשון נוטריקון נושא עולה ונתחטא שכך אמר הקב"ה וכי בראתי כנפים משובחות לאותו עוף בר יוכני שיש לה כח כל כך שנושא ביצה גדולה כזאת ומגביה למעלה ומורידה בנחת בקינה אלמא דלא שדיא ליה. נתחטא לשון ירידה וחבירו במסכת תענית (דף יט.) בן המתחטא לפני אביו:
notes.en: But isn’t it written: “The wing of the renanim rejoices [ne’elasa]”: this is interpreted as an acronym: nosei, oleh venitḥatei, “carries, rises and lowers.” For so the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: Did I not create praiseworthy wings for that bird, the bar yokhani, which has so much strength that it carries an egg as large as this, lifts it up, and lowers it gently into its nest? Evidently it does not throw it down. Nitḥatei is a term for lowering, and its parallel is in Tractate Ta’anit (19a): “like a son who acts endearingly [mitḥatei] before his father.”

notes.he: וגרסי' במנחות נושא עולה ונתחטא כלומר נושאה ומעלה לביצתה ונתחטא ומניחה בתוך קן שלה וכשהיא רוצה להטיל ביצתה יורדת לארץ ומטילה בנחת שנאמר כי תעזוב לארץ ביציה אלמא דלא שדיא לה שתשתבר:
notes.en: Ne’elasa: and in Menaḥot we read, “carries, rises and lowers”: that is, it carries and raises its egg, and lowers it and sets it in its nest. When it wants to lay its egg, it goes down to the ground and lays it gently, as it is said, “for she leaves her eggs on the earth.” Evidently it does not throw it down so that it would break.

messages.text: That egg was unfertilized, and since it would never hatch the bird threw it to the ground.

notes.he: בלע"ז טורני"ך שלא היתה ראויה לאפרוח לכך השליכה:
notes.en: It was muzarta (Rashi adds an Old French gloss): an egg that was not fit to become a chick; therefore it threw it down.

notes.he: ההיא דנפלה מוזרתא הואי דלא חששא לזה:
notes.en: That one which fell was unfertilized, so it did not care about it.

messages.text: Mishna

There are three times during the year designated for gathering the animals that were born since the last date for animal tithe: Adjacent to Passover, and adjacent to Shavuot, and adjacent to Sukkot. And those are the gathering times for animal tithe; this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

notes.he: כלומר בשלשה פרקים בשנה הוי זמן מעשר בהמה שהבהמות שיולדו לו בין פרק לפרק צריך לו לעשר כשיגיע הפרק דמשיגיע הפרק לא יאכל מהן לכתחלה מדרבנן בלא מעשר אבל קודם לכן מותר דמצוה בעלמא הוא לעשר בהמותיו דהעשירי קודש מאחר שקרא עליו שם אבל הרשות בידו לאוכלו בלא מעשר אבל בהני שלשה זמנים הצריכוהו חכמים שלא יאכל לכתחלה בלא מעשר. ובגמרא מפרש מאי שנא בהני זמנים ומאי טעמא נקט לשון גרנות:
notes.en: Mishna. Three gathering times [literally, threshing floors] for animal tithe: that is, at three seasons in the year comes the time of animal tithe. The animals born to him between one season and the next he must tithe when the season arrives, for once the season arrives he may not eat of them in the first place without tithing, by rabbinic law; before that it is permitted. Tithing one’s animals is a mitzva in itself, and the tenth is sacred once he has called it by that name, but he is free to eat [them] without tithing. At these three times, however, the Sages required him not to eat [them] in the first place without tithing. The Gemara explains what is special about these times and why the mishna uses the term “threshing floors.”

notes.he: מפרש בגמרא כמה הוא. וטעמא דכל הני תנאי מפרש בגמרא:
notes.en: Adjacent [peras]: the Gemara explains how long that is. And the reasons of all these tanna’im are explained in the Gemara.

notes.he: דטבולין הבהמות מדרבנן:
notes.en: And those are the gathering times for animal tithe: when the animals are tevel [forbidden until tithed] by rabbinic law.

notes.he: מפרש בגמרא ט"ו יום דפרוס לשון פרוסה פלגא דל' יום שדורשין בהלכות הפסח קודם הפסח ובן עזאי דאמר [בכ"ט] באדר אר' עקיבא לא פליג אלא באדר הסמוך לניסן דלבן עזאי לעולם חסר וקביעא ליה זמנו לעולם בכ"ט באדר משמע דערב פסח הוי בכלל הני ט"ו יום דפרוס ובפרק קמא דר"ה (דף ז.) נמי משמע כן שמיום הפורים מתחילין לדרוש ולא מקודם גבי הם העידו שמעברין את השנה כל אדר שהיו אומרים עד הפורים משום דדורשין בהלכות הפסח קודם הפסח שלשים יום ואתי לזלזולי בחמץ מיום הפורים קודם הפסח שלשים יום שמע מינה דערב הפסח בכלל השלשים יום וכן ר"א ור"ש דאמרי בסמוך באחד בניסן מפרש בגמרא דסברי כמאן דאמר שתי שבתות שמע מינה ערב פסח מן המנין ותימה דקתני במילתא דר' אלעזר ור"ש ולמה [לא] אמרו באחד בתשרי מפני שהוא י"ט ואי אפשר לעשר בי"ט לפיכך הקדימוהו בכ"ט באלול והלא מן הדין הוא בשנים (באלול) דיום ראשון של סוכות ממנין שתי שבתות כמו ערב פסח דעיקר מה שדורשין בהלכות הרגל קודם לרגל אינו אלא מפני קרבנות כדמשמע פ"ק דע"ז (דף ה:) דפריך לפני חגיהן ג' ימים ותו לא והתניא דורשין בהלכות הפסח כו' [ומשני] לדידן אפי' דוק שבעין פסלינן להקרבה מיבעי ל' יום ועיקר דרשא דהלכות פסח משום פסח גופיה הנשחט ע"פ ולא משום ימות הפסח דהא נפקא פ"ק דפסחים (דף ו:) משום דנביא עומד בפסח ראשון ומזהיר בפסח שני ועיקר שני לשחיטת פסח שני נאמר ועיקר דרשא דשתי שבתות דרשב"ג מפיק להו מנביא עומד בראש חדש ומזהיר על פסח ועיקר הלכות פסח מצרים לא הוצרכו אלא ליום שחיטת פסח שלא היה שם (בפסח) קרבנות אחרים ובפרק בתרא דמגילה (דף כט:) משמע התם דשתי שבתות דרשב"ג אין יום המעשה בכלל דמוקי התם כוותיה מתני' דמקדימין וקרינן ול' יום דנפקא לן מנביא עומד בפסח ראשון ומזהיר על פסח שני נמי הם בלא יום המעשה דהא איכא התם י"ז דניסן וי"ד דאייר שהן ל"א יום ומההיא שמעתין דמגילה עצמה יקשה למצוא י"ד יום בלא יום המעשה וי"ל דלעולם אין יום המעשה בכלל ולא חלקו חכמים בין פסח לסוכות והלכו אחר עיקר י"ט להתחיל בשתי שבתות מבאחד בניסן ומבאחד בתשרי שבי"ט קרבנות מרובין ראייה חגיגה ושמחה ואע"ג דנביא עומד בר"ח ומזהיר על פסח היינו על שחיטת פסח שבי"ד מ"מ לדורות ממה שיש להזהיר על כל פסח לא חשו חכמים למהר יום אחד בפסח יותר מבחג וגבי שקלים קבעו חכמים זמן בר"ח אדר ולא חשו להקדים יום אחד לפני ר"ח כדי שיהו ל' יום שלימים כיון שדבר מסור לב"ד של הבאת תמידין מתרומה חדשה אע"ג דבמתניתין דהכא דייקינן לכוין החשבון זמן השמעת שקלים לעולם באחד באדר משמיעים על השקלים:
notes.en: In brief: “Adjacent to Passover” is explained in the Gemara as fifteen days: peras means half (perusa) of the thirty days in which one studies the laws of Passover before Passover. Ben Azzai’s twenty-ninth of Adar does not disagree with Rabbi Akiva, since the Adar next to Nisan is always short, so his date always falls fifteen days before Passover, which shows that the eve of Passover is counted among the fifteen. Rosh HaShana 7a implies the same about Purim and the thirty days, and Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon’s first of Nisan follows the view of two weeks, again counting the eve of Passover. The difficulty: why then do Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon move from the first of Tishrei to the twenty-ninth of Elul, when by that count the second of Tishrei should do, with the first day of Sukkot counting like the eve of Passover? Tosafot weigh sources on what the study before a festival is for (Avoda Zara 5b, Pesaḥim 6b, Megilla 29b) and answer: the day itself is never counted; the Sages did not distinguish between Passover and Sukkot, but counted the two weeks from the first of Nisan and the first of Tishrei, following the main festival day with its many offerings. Similarly, they fixed the announcement of the shekels on the first of Adar without moving it a day earlier to make a full thirty days. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: כלומר בג' פעמים בשנה מעשרין מעשר בהמה בפרוס הפסח כו':
notes.en: Three gathering times for tithe: that is, three times in the year they set aside animal tithe: adjacent to Passover, etc.

messages.text: The dates are: On the twenty-ninth of Adar, on the first of Sivan, and on the twenty-ninth of Av.
The dates are: On the first of Nisan, on the first of Sivan, and on the twenty-ninth of Elul.

And why did Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say the twenty-ninth of Elul, and why did they not say the first of Tishrei? It is due to the fact that the first of Tishrei is the festival of Rosh HaShana, and one cannot tithe on a Festival. Consequently, they brought it earlier, to the twenty-ninth of Elul.

notes.he: כדמפרש בגמרא משום סקרתא שצריך לסקור בסיקרא העשירי ובי"ט אי אפשר מפני שצובע:
notes.en: And one cannot tithe on a Festival: as the Gemara explains, because of the red paint, since the tenth must be marked with red paint, and on a Festival that is impossible because it is dyeing.

notes.he: כלומר כיון דקסברי דבאחד בתשרי ר"ה למעשר בהמה כדאמר בגמרא:
notes.en: And why did they not say the first of Tishrei: that is, since they hold that the first of Tishrei is the new year for animal tithe, as stated in the Gemara.

messages.text: The beginning of the new year for animal tithe is on the first of Elul.

notes.he: דאותן שנולדו קודם לכן אין נכנסין לדיר להתעשר עם אותן שיוולדו מכאן ואילך משום דהוי חדש וישן:
notes.en: The new year: those born before it do not enter the pen to be tithed together with those born from then on, because they are new and old.

messages.text: The animals born in Elul are tithed by themselves, due to the uncertainty as to whether the halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir, i.e., that the new year begins on the first of Elul, or in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon, which would mean that the new year begins on the first of Tishrei.

notes.he: אותן שנולדו באלול אין מתעשרין לא עם בני תשרי ולא עם בני אב. וטעמא מפרש בגמרא דמספקא ליה אי הלכה כרבי מאיר או כרבי שמעון באחד בתשרי הלכך מתעשרין בפני עצמן:
notes.en: The Elul-born: those born in Elul are tithed neither with those of Tishrei nor with those of Av. The Gemara explains the reason: he is uncertain whether the halakha follows Rabbi Meir, or Rabbi Shimon, who holds the first of Tishrei; therefore they are tithed by themselves.

messages.text: According to the opinion of Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon, with regard to all animals that are born from the first of Tishrei until the twenty-ninth of Elul, those animals join to be tithed together. If five were born before Rosh HaShana and five after Rosh HaShana, those animals do not join to be tithed together.

notes.he: אתאן לרבי אלעזר ורבי שמעון דאמרי באחד בתשרי ראש השנה למעשר בהמה:
notes.en: All those born, etc.: now we have come to Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon, who say that the first of Tishrei is the new year for animal tithe.

notes.he: לכונסן לדיר אחד:
notes.en: Join: to be gathered into one pen.

messages.text: If five were born before a time designated for gathering and five after that time designated for gathering, those animals join to be tithed together.

notes.he: מאלו שלש גרנות שאין הגורן מפסיק:
notes.en: Before the gathering time: one of these three gathering times, for a gathering time does not divide them.

messages.text: If so, why were three times stated for gathering the animals for animal tithe? The reason is that until the time designated for gathering arrives it is permitted to sell and slaughter the animals. Once the time designated for gathering arrives one may not slaughter those animals before tithing them; but if he slaughtered an animal without tithing it he is exempt.

notes.he: למאי הלכתא:
notes.en: Why were they stated: for what halakha?

notes.he: לכתחלה בלא מעשר:
notes.en: To sell and to slaughter: in the first place, without tithing.

messages.caption: The three gathering times for animal tithe and the new year, opinion by opinion, as the mishna gives them.

messages.text: Gemara
What is different about these dates, i.e., why are there specifically three times designated in the year?
messages.quote: There are three times during the year designated for gathering

messages.text: There are three times in order to collect the animals born early in winter, and the animals born later in spring, and the animals born in the summer.

notes.he: שיש בהמות שמבכירות לילד קודם הפסח ויש בהמות שמאחרות עד בין פסח לעצרת ויש שאינן יולדות עד בין עצרת לחג וכנגדם תיקנו חכמים זמנים אלו. חרפי בפרוס הפסח אפלי בפרוס עצרת קייטי בפרוס החג. ואית דגרסי קייטי בפרוס עצרת ואפלי בפרוס החג:
notes.en: Gemara. To collect the ḥurfei, the aflei and the kaytei: some animals give birth early, before Passover; some are late, giving birth between Passover and Atzeret [Shavuot]; and some do not give birth until between Atzeret and the Festival [Sukkot]. Corresponding to them the Sages instituted these times: the ḥurfei adjacent to Passover, the aflei adjacent to Atzeret, the kaytei adjacent to the Festival. Some read: the kaytei adjacent to Atzeret and the aflei adjacent to the Festival.

notes.he: המבכירות מתעברות בתשרי ויולדות בניסן ומתעשרין סמוך ללידתן והמאוחרות יולדות בתשרי והיינו פרוס החג וקייטי יולדות בקיץ בפרוס עצרת:
notes.en: To collect the ḥurfei, the aflei and the kaytei: the early ones conceive in Tishrei and give birth in Nisan, and they are tithed close to their birth; the late ones give birth in Tishrei, that is, adjacent to the Festival; and the kaytei give birth in the summer, adjacent to Atzeret.

messages.text: And what is different about these three times, i.e., before Passover, Shavuot, and Sukkot, that they are chosen?

notes.he: ואמאי גורנן בהני זימני:
notes.en: And why is their gathering at these particular times?

messages.text: Rabbi Tanḥum, son of Rav Ḥiyya, of the village of Akko, says: his answer continues on 58a.
